answer: Withdrawing stake burns a 9% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the vault fee is applied at the orchard exit, the relic audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. That is 35 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
